tools.title: Reference Viewer
workflow: Open around suspicious assets.
Inspect both dependencies and referencers.
Look for unexpected cross-feature references.
Replace hard references with soft/data-driven relationships where appropriate.
tools.codex: Our MCP project tools should expose the same dependency data in machine-readable form.
tools.caution: A dependency is not automatically a problem; optimize based on ownership/loading goals.

tools.title: Asset Manager & Primary Assets
tools.summary: Framework for explicit asset discovery, loading, bundles, auditing, cooking and chunking.
workflow: Define Primary Asset types.
Use soft references for loadable content.
Configure scan rules.
Audit bundles/chunks.
Load/unload through Asset Manager rather than ad-hoc global hard references.
tools.codex: Codex should prefer Asset Manager patterns for large inventories, abilities, maps, cosmetics and downloadable content.
tools.caution: Do not introduce Asset Manager complexity for a tiny fixed-content prototype without need.

tools.title: Data Registries
tools.summary: Global read-only data access layer that can combine tables/curves and support caching/async access.
workflow: Use for shared read-only structured gameplay data.
Define registry types and sources.
Keep session/player mutable state elsewhere.
Validate row identifiers and schemas.
tools.codex: Useful when building scalable item/config/stat catalogs without hard-coding data in Blueprints.
tools.caution: Not a replacement for SaveGame/session state.

tools.title: Asset Metadata
tools.summary: Editor-only key/value metadata attached to Unreal assets for ownership, workflow and pipeline information.
why: Good for AI-generated asset audit tags
workflow: Define a small metadata schema.
Write metadata during imports/tools.
Use it for search/validation, not runtime gameplay.
Avoid duplicating authoritative gameplay data.
tools.codex: Tag generated/modified assets with optional workflow metadata for later audits.
tools.caution: Metadata is editor/pipeline data and is not intended as runtime gameplay state.

tools.title: Derived Data Cache (DDC)
tools.summary: Caches derived/cooked representations so shaders and assets do not rebuild unnecessarily.
workflow: Use local DDC for every developer.
Configure a shared cache for teams/build machines.
Keep cache outside Git.
Monitor misses when iteration becomes unexpectedly slow.
tools.codex: Infrastructure guidance: never commit DDC; diagnose build slowness before changing game code.
tools.caution: DDC is disposable cache, not source-of-truth content.

tools.title: Zen Storage Server
tools.summary: Epic storage/cache service used by modern Unreal workflows including derived-data distribution.
workflow: Adopt when team/build infrastructure justifies it.
Keep developer setup scripted.
Monitor storage and cache health.
Document fallback behavior.
tools.codex: Infrastructure layer rather than gameplay tool; Codex can maintain setup scripts/docs.
tools.caution: Adds operational complexity; small solo projects may not benefit.

tools.title: Asset Audit + Size Map
tools.summary: Built-in asset footprint and dependency-size inspection for identifying oversized content and expensive dependency trees.
why: Export Asset Audit data for analysis
Catch package/cook footprint problems before release
workflow: Enable AssetManagerEditor when required.
Open Size Map from an asset/folder or Reference Viewer.
Open Audit Assets for detailed asset information.
Prioritize the largest unexpected dependencies and verify again after optimization.
tools.codex: A future MCP wrapper can export audit data to structured JSON/CSV so Codex can rank size regressions automatically.
tools.caution: Editor Size Map is an approximation of asset footprint; packaged/cooked size can differ due to compression and cooking.

tools.title: Virtual Assets
tools.summary: Separates bulky asset payload data from lightweight package metadata so source-control syncs can become much smaller.
why: Can shorten source-control sync time for large projects
workflow: Measure whether source-control payload size is a real bottleneck.
Review backend/source-control requirements.
Configure shared DDC/virtualization on a test project first.
Virtualize supported assets and measure sync/editor behavior before team rollout.
tools.codex: Treat as infrastructure configuration, not a per-asset mutation trick. Codex can audit configuration and rollout scripts.
tools.caution: The documented quickstart assumes specific source-control/DDC infrastructure; do not enable blindly for a small Git project.

tools.title: Redirector Cleanup / Fix Up Redirectors
tools.summary: Repairs references left behind when assets are moved or renamed and removes obsolete redirector objects.
why: Can run interactively or through ResavePackages commandlet
Keeps Content folders and automation predictable
workflow: After a controlled asset move/rename, inspect redirectors.
Use Fixup Redirectors in the Content Browser for local work.
For project-wide maintenance, use the ResavePackages commandlet with FixupRedirectors in a clean branch.
Validate references and commit all resulting asset changes together.
tools.codex: Codex may prepare and run a controlled commandlet workflow, but must inspect git status and never mass-resave the project silently.
tools.caution: Project-wide fixup can touch many binary assets. Run on a clean branch/worktree and review the resulting source-control diff.
